title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum

statement.hi:
Binary tree ka `root` diya hai. **Path** = nodes ka sequence jisme har adjacent pair ke beech edge ho; ek node path me ek hi baar aa sakta hai, aur path ka root se guzarna zaroori nahi. Path me kam se kam ek node hona chahiye.

Kisi bhi non-empty path ka **maximum path sum** (nodes ki values ka sum) return karo.
statement.en:
Given the `root` of a binary tree: a **path** is a sequence of nodes where each adjacent pair is joined by an edge; a node appears at most once, and the path need not pass through the root. A path has at least one node.

Return the **maximum path sum** (sum of node values) of any non-empty path.

hi: Har node ke liye do cheezein socho: (1) is node se neeche jaane wala best "single branch" sum, (2) is node pe mudne wala best path.
Negative branch lene ka koi fayda nahi — `max(0, gain)` lo.
Saari values negative ho sakti hain; answer ko `INT_MIN` / root ki value se initialise karo.
en: For each node, think of two things: (1) the best single downward branch starting there, (2) the best path that turns at that node.
A negative branch never helps — use `max(0, gain)`.
All values may be negative; initialise the answer to `INT_MIN` / the root value.

approach.hi:
`gain(node)` = node se neeche jaane wali best single branch ka sum = `val + max(0, gain(left), gain(right))` (negative branch chhod do).
Usi DFS me, node pe mudne wala path `val + max(0, gainL) + max(0, gainR)` hai — isse global `best` update karo.
Har node ek baar: O(n) time, O(h) stack.
approach.en:
`gain(node)` = the best single downward branch from the node = `val + max(0, gain(left), gain(right))` (drop negative branches).
In the same DFS, the path turning at the node is `val + max(0, gainL) + max(0, gainR)` — update a global `best` with it.
Each node once: O(n) time, O(h) stack.
